Keter

The first generation. Where Yaju Agent Systems began, and everything it could not do yet.

Keter — Version 1.0

The first build of Yaju Agent Systems. A bare runtime that could execute one agent, and very little else.


  • Single agent per workspace

  • No cost visibility

  • No external integrations

  • Raw logs, no real monitoring

Keter — Version 1.1

The origin of Yaju Agent Systems as a product. Our first released version still lacked most of what we offer today.


  • No efficient agent management

  • No cost visibility

  • No external integrations

  • No advanced agent monitoring

Keter — Version 1.2

Introduced the agent catalogue, so teams could finally see what was actually running across the organization.


  • One catalogue for every agent

  • Still no owner per agent

  • No cost visibility

  • No external integrations

Keter — Version 1.3

Gave every agent a unique identity and a named owner, ending the first wave of shadow agents.


  • Unique ID for every agent

  • A named owner per agent

  • No credential handling yet

  • No policy at runtime

Keter — Version 1.4

The first credential store, so keys stopped living in repositories, config files and shell history.


  • Central credential store

  • Secrets out of agent code

  • Manual rotation only

  • No access rules yet

Keter — Version 1.5

Added run history, the first step towards understanding what an agent had actually done.


  • Persistent run history

  • Inputs and outputs captured

  • No tool-level detail

  • No exportable record

Keter — Version 1.6

Brought the command line, so engineers could deploy and inspect without ever opening a dashboard.


  • CLI for deploy and inspect

  • Runs inside CI/CD pipelines

  • Partial parity with the dashboard

  • Still no policy enforcement

Keter — Version 1.7

The last Keter release. Stable and genuinely useful, but clearly limited by having no governance layer.


  • Stable multi-agent execution

  • Credentials and run history

  • No policy enforced at runtime

  • No cost attribution

Nahar

The second generation. Governance and observability arrive: policy at runtime, and a trace for every run.

Nahar — Version 2.0

The second generation opens with a policy engine that runs at the moment of action, not in a document.


  • Policy enforced at runtime

  • Access rules per agent and user

  • Credentials resolved per call

  • No spend attribution yet

Nahar — Version 2.1

Full session tracing arrives: every model call, tool invocation, input and output captured as the run happens.


  • Complete session traces

  • Naharable in real time

  • Tool-level detail

  • Traces not yet exportable

Nahar — Version 2.2

Made the record immutable and exportable, so evidence could leave the platform intact for an auditor.


  • Immutable audit trail

  • Timestamp and acting user

  • Exportable on demand

  • No automatic quality checks

Nahar — Version 2.3

Added human approval gates, pausing the runtime before anything irreversible could happen.


  • Approval gates on risky actions

  • Bounded loops and retry limits

  • Outside agents inherit policy

  • Still no cost controls

Oran

The current generation. Cost control, optimization and the capabilities organizations run on today.

Oran — Version 3.1

The third generation begins with the question nobody could answer before: what does each agent actually cost?


  • Spend attributed per agent

  • Breakdown by user and model

  • Reported in dollars, not tokens

  • Reporting only, no limits

Oran — Version 3.2

Turned visibility into control with circuit-breaker budgets that stop an overrun instead of reporting it later.


  • Hard limits per workspace and team

  • Warning at 80 percent

  • Automatic block at 100 percent

  • Forecast for the rest of the cycle

Oran — Version 3.3

Evals arrive, turning passive logging into active quality enforcement on every single run.


  • Behavioural and structural checks

  • Latency and cost criteria

  • Halts an agent on a failed check

  • Scores every run automatically

Oran — Version 3.4

Optimizer closes the cost loop, cutting spend without letting quality slip on your own benchmarks.


  • Model and prompt optimization

  • Tool trimming

  • Hybrid agent conversion

  • Measured against your own evals

Oran — Version 3.5

Made agents reusable across the organization instead of being rebuilt from scratch inside every team.


  • Agent Hub and internal catalogue

  • Browse, fork, publish, improve

  • Versioning and one-command rollback

  • Skills shared between teams

Oran — Version 3.6

NEW

Our latest and most capable version, giving organizations what they need to automate work with AI agents efficiently.


  • Multiple integrations

  • Agent situation awareness

  • Advanced agent management

  • Cost visibility and control
